Six variants on a z-bucket. 6 MHz SAM, MODE 4, 120,000 T-states
between 50 Hz interrupts. Opaque box, whole, a window every
fourth row - no row program and no dispatcher anywhere.

  z   size        box  drawn  T-states   T/byte  % frame     code

  1   44x55      1210    598     11837      9.8     9.9%     1904
  2   28x35       490    252      5341     10.9     4.5%      890
  3   20x25       250    126      2979     11.9     2.5%      501
  4   12x15        90     54      1373     15.3     1.1%      247
  5   8x10         40     24       799     20.0     0.7%      151

  Holding still in a bucket: the draw, plus the L the sprite
  leaves as it moves (scaled with the bucket, 4 bytes and 8 rows
  a frame at the top).

  z   size          draw    the L   a frame  % frame  how many
  0   64x80        22489     5986     28475    23.7%       4.2

  Crossing a boundary. Growing costs nothing - the bigger box
  swallows the smaller one. Shrinking leaves a ring, and with
  two buffers the ring has to be cleared in both, so it is paid
  on the crossing frame and the one after it.

  boundary          ring  clear it  and draw of steady  % frame
  64x80 -> 44x55    1350     12691     24528      1.5x    20.4%
  44x55 -> 28x35     720      7186     12527      1.7x    10.4%
  28x35 -> 20x25     240      3516      6495      1.5x     5.4%
  20x25 -> 12x15     160      2448      3821      1.7x     3.2%
  12x15 -> 8x10       50      1504      2303      1.6x     1.9%

  The other way to cross: draw the smaller picture inside the
  box it is leaving for those two frames, so there is no ring at
  all - one extra compiled form a boundary.
